# A Secret Habit?

> "Have no fellowship with the unfruitful deeds of darkness, but rather even reprove them."
>
> — Ephesians 5:11

Nobody has ever called this a social habit. You don't do it at a dinner party. It may be the most private thing you do, and that privacy is what keeps it going.

The other two faces of lust live the same way. Nobody watches porn at the dinner table. And the messages to her are the ones you delete.

Your mind, your drive and your soul are the real reasons to stop, and they always were. You never needed a study to tell you so. The first week you did it as a boy, you locked the door. Nobody taught you to hide it.

You knew.

## What the secret does {-}

**It makes every man think he's the only one.** You saw this with the church guy. A whole row of men, each sure the others are clean. If they compared notes for five minutes the spell would break. A nineteen-year-old wrote of his own years in that row: "I harboured a wrong notion that I was the only guy with these special problems."

**It protects the lies.** A lie kept in your head never has to face a question. Said aloud, it sounds as thin as it is. Try telling another grown man, with a straight face, "I need this in order to sleep."

**It splits you in two.** There's the man people meet, and there's the man behind the door. The first spends a lot of energy making sure nobody meets the second. One coach doesn't think the wall holds anyway: "the things you do in private come out in public". And C.S. Lewis, in the letter you read in the last chapter, saw what the wall does to the man behind it. For Lewis, "almost the main work of life is to come out of our selves, out of the little dark prison we are all born in." A secret is that prison with the bolt on the inside.

**It sets you against your own side.** A secret has to be guarded against somebody. This one is guarded against the people who are for you: your partner, your friends, your children. So you end up keeping watch against your own family. That is a small disloyalty, repeated every day. The free man is finished with it. He is on the same side as the people who love him.

A man with a secret can't be fully known. And he never feels fully loved, because he's always thinking, "You wouldn't say that if you knew."

## Into the light {-}

Two verses after the one that opens this chapter, Paul goes on: "But all things, when they are reproved, are revealed by the light, for everything that reveals is light."

In the dark this habit looks big, and it looks like yours alone. In the light it's a small, dull thing that millions of men do, for no gain at all.

You've been bringing it into the light since page one. Every chapter has taken one more piece of it out and looked at it. That's why it's shrinking.

A Christian therapist has been free of this himself for nearly forty years, and has spent those years helping other men out. He puts the rule in one sentence: "Masturbation is a secret and as long as it stays a secret, you will probably not get better." He isn't theorizing. His own freedom began the day he said it aloud to another student: "the first step in that process was telling my roommate when I was in school. And from that moment on, it started to break off my life."

A pastor says the same thing in seven words: "You're only as strong as you are honest."

A Christian counselor draws a line worth remembering. "Godly sorrow" is Paul's phrase for the kind of regret that turns a man around. The counselor says, "Godly sorrow doesn't fear that people will find out about your sin." The dread of being found out isn't repentance. It's the habit guarding itself.

When to tell another person, and whom, comes up again later in the book. For now, do one thing first. Stop hiding it from yourself, and stop hiding it from God. He has seen every time, and he hasn't left. If you're not a believer, say the plain facts aloud in an empty room, and notice how much smaller they sound.

Every day more men walk out into the light. The ones left behind get more afraid of being the last.

**DON'T BE THE LAST MAN IN THE DARK.**
